title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE PERFORMANCE OF DUTIES BY MILITARY POLICE
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Act on the Performance of Duties by Military Police and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Military police) "Persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 1 of Article 3 of the Act on the Performance of Duties by Military Police (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means persons appointed as military police by the Minister of National Defense or the Chief of Staff of each military service (in the case of the Marine Corps, referring to the Commandant of the Marine Corps; hereinafter the same shall apply) according to the classifications set forth in the following subparagraphs; provided, in the case of enlisted members, it means persons appointed as military police by the commander of the unit in which a military police unit is established:
  1. Persons belonging to the Ministry of National Defense, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, or units or agencies directly under the Ministry of National Defense: the Minister of National Defense;
  2. Persons belonging to the Army, Navy (including the Marine Corps), or Air Force: the Chief of Staff of each military service.

Article 3 (Identification) The Minister of National Defense and the Chief of Staff of each military service shall issue identification verifying military-police status to persons appointed as military police pursuant to Article 2 (excluding enlisted members).

Article 4 (Military police gear) "Devices and instruments prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as handcuffs, ropes, police batons, electronic shock devices, electronic shock guns, and shields" in subparagraph 5 of Article 3 of the Act means the following devices and instruments:
  1. Devices: wearable photographing, video-recording, and audio-recording devices;
  2. Instruments: Handcuffs, ropes, police batons, electronic shock devices, electronic shock guns, shields, protective gear such as helmets, and rubber bullet guns.

Article 5 (Reporting) Where any of the following cases occurs, military police shall report the relevant fact to the commander of the unit in which a military police unit is established:
  1. Where military police have cooperated with the Military Human Rights Protection Officer pursuant to Article 6 of the Act;
  2. Where military police have requested accompaniment pursuant to Article 7(2) of the Act;
  3. Where military police have conducted an investigation concerning the possession of weapons or deadly weapons pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Act;
  4. Where military police have issued a warning for the prevention of a criminal act or suppressed a criminal act pursuant to Article 8 of the Act;
  5. Where military police have entered another person’s land, building, vessel, or vehicle pursuant to Article 9(1) of the Act;
  6. Where military police have used hazardous military police equipment pursuant to Article 11 of the Act;
  7. Where military police have used sprayers, etc. pursuant to Article 13 of the Act.

Article 6 (Cooperation from relevant agencies for performance of duties by military police) Where necessary for performing duties under Article 5(1)3 of the Act, military police may request cooperation from relevant agencies, such as police agencies, regarding the transfer of custody, transfer of cases, and fact-finding inquiries.

Article 7 (Command and supervision of military police) The commander of a unit in which a military police unit is established shall guarantee the independence of military police when military police perform duties under Article 5(1)3 of the Act in order to ensure the fairness of investigations.

Article 8 (Maintenance of traffic, operation, and navigation order) (1) Before conducting a crackdown under Article 10(1) of the Act, military police shall present identification verifying their status under Article 3 to the person subject to the crackdown.
  (2) Where military police conduct crackdown activities under Article 10(2) of the Act, they shall prepare a sobriety crackdown report in Form 1.
  (3) Matters necessary for detailed procedures and methods of crackdown activities and the handling of crackdown results, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be determined by the Minister of National Defense.

Article 9 (Types of hazardous military police equipment) The types of hazardous military police equipment under the proviso to Article 11(1) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. Weapons;
  2. Handcuffs;
  3. Ropes;
  4. Police batons;
  5. Electronic shock devices;
  6. Electronic shock guns;
  7. Rubber bullet guns;
  8. Tear gas agents and devices for launching such agents.

Article 10 (Safety training on hazardous military police equipment and military police equipment) The standards for safety training on hazardous military police equipment pursuant to the proviso to Article 11(1) of the Act and the contents and methods of training on the use, management, and safety, etc. of military police equipment pursuant to Article 15(1) of the Act shall be as prescribed in Appendix 1, respectively.

Article 11 (Standards for safety inspection of hazardous military police equipment) The standards for safety inspection of hazardous military police equipment under the proviso to Articles 11(1) and 15(2) of the Act shall be as prescribed in Appendix 2, respectively.

Article 12 (Standards for use of hazardous military police equipment) The standards for use of hazardous military police equipment pursuant to Article 11(3) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. In cases of handcuffs and ropes: They shall be used only to the minimum extent necessary in any of the following cases:
  a. Where necessary to escort or detain, in accordance with procedures prescribed by statutes, a person against whom an arrest warrant or detention warrant is executed or who has received a judgment or disposition restricting physical freedom;
  b. Where necessary to prevent a criminal, intoxicated person, or mentally disturbed person from attempting suicide or self-injury;
  2. In cases of police batons: Care shall be taken to minimize harm to life or body;
  3. In cases of electronic shock devices, electronic shock guns, and rubber bullet guns: An electric shock shall not be administered toward the other party's face, and electrode darts or rubber bullets shall not be fired toward the other party's face;
  4. In cases of tear gas agents and devices for launching such agents: They shall be used only to the minimum extent necessary in any of the following cases. In such cases, a launch angle of at least 30 degrees shall be maintained, and such agents shall not be launched toward the other party's face from a distance of less than 1 meter:
  a. Where necessary to arrest a criminal or prevent escape;
  b. Where necessary to protect the life or body of another person or military police;
  c. Where necessary to suppress resistance against the performance of official duties.

Article 13 (Safety inspection of newly introduced hazardous military police equipment) (1) Where the Minister of National Defense intends to newly introduce hazardous military police equipment, the Minister shall conduct a safety inspection under Article 11(4) of the Act to evaluate the effects of the hazardous military police equipment to be newly introduced (hereafter in this Article referred to as "equipment proposed for introduction") on human life or body.
  (2) A safety inspection under paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with inspection methods and standards proposed by external experts in fields related to the equipment proposed for introduction based on the major characteristics or operating principles of such equipment. In such cases, where there are generally recognized reasonable inspection methods or standards applicable to the equipment proposed for introduction, the safety inspection may be conducted in accordance with such methods or standards.
  (3) Under the latter part of Article 11(4) of the Act, an external expert who participates in a safety inspection shall submit to the Minister of National Defense an opinion on whether the equipment proposed for introduction is safe within 30 days from the date the safety inspection is completed.
  (4) The Minister of National Defense shall submit a safety inspection result report containing the following matters to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly within 3 months from the date the safety inspection on the equipment proposed for introduction is conducted under the former part of Article 11(4) of the Act:
  1. Major characteristics and basic operating principles of the equipment proposed for introduction;
  2. Methods and standards for the safety inspection;
  3. Opinions of external experts who participated in the safety inspection;
  4. Results of the safety inspection and comprehensive opinions.

Article 22-2 (Digitization of military criminal justice procedures) (1) The Minister of National Defense shall establish and operate an information system (referring to an electronic management system constructed by combining hardware, software, databases, networks, security elements, etc., for use in the creation, acquisition, storage, transmission, and reception of data in the military; hereinafter referred to as "Military Justice Information System") to support the efficient processing of various data and information necessary for implementing prompt, fair, and transparent military criminal justice procedures and the digitization of recording and management duties. In such cases, the Minister of National Defense may establish and operate a service portal related to military justice (hereinafter referred to as "Information Portal") so that the public may easily and promptly access data (referring to data processed by electronic means and expressed in signs, letters, voices, sounds, or images, etc.) created, acquired, or managed using the Military Justice Information System.
  (2) The head of a unit in which a military police unit is established shall support necessary measures so that a military judicial police officer under subparagraph 1 of Article 43 of the Military Court Act or an assistant military judicial police officer under subparagraph 1 of Article 46 of that Act may utilize the Military Justice Information System and the Information Portal for relevant duties in order to efficiently perform the duties under Article 5(1)3 of the Act (limited to investigations).
  (3) Matters necessary for the operation and management of the Military Justice Information System and the Information Portal, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be determined by the Minister of National Defense.
  [This Article Added on Feb. 10, 2026]

Article 23 (Processing of sensitive information and unique identifying information) (1) Where unavoidable for performing duties under Article 5(1)3 of the Act (excluding duties relating to the collection of criminal information; hereafter in this paragraph the same shall apply) and Article 5(1)4 of the Act, military police may process materials containing information classified as follows: <Amended on Feb. 10, 2026>
  1. Duties under Article 5(1)3 of the Act: Information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act, and resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver’s license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of that Decree;
  2. Duties under Article 5(1)4 of the Act: Information concerning health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act, information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act, and resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver’s license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of that Decree.
  (2) Where unavoidable for performing business affairs relating to the operation and management, etc. of the Military Justice Information System, the Minister of National Defense and the head of a unit under Article 22-2(2) may process materials containing information classified as follows: <Added on Feb. 10, 2026>
  1. Military Justice Information System: Information concerning health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act, information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act, and resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver’s license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of that Decree;
  2. Information Portal: Resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act.
